newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 13.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech economy is seen in a more positive light among foreign economists than in the eyes of domestic critics.

- The account balance of Ostrava's Union Banka exceeded, in the first three quarters of the year, expectations for the whole year, reaching 16.49 billion crowns. The main reason is the bank's growing reputation as a medium-sized bank and its fusion with Skala, Ekoagrobanka and Evrobanka.

- The import of food and agricultural products has increased quickly this year, while exports have actually declined. Thus a number of Czech producers are calling for more protection of the domestic market.
- A law currently being presented in parliament calls for a fifteen percent increase of the consumer tax on tobacco products.

- After a decrease in August, food prices increased once again in September, though not as much as in September last year. Retirees, whose cost of living for food has increased by 20.1 percent since December, 1995, will feel the increase the most.

- Metalimex a.s., which placed second on the list of the top 100 companies in the Czech Republic, wants to return to the natural gas industry after a year-long pause. The company does not plan to import gas as it has done in the past, but go directly to the end user, according to the company's general manager, Petr Paukner.

- After the government's July decision to privatise the National Property Fund's remaining 31.5 percent of Moravske Naftove Doly Hodonin a.s., the company is now becoming a wholly private company. The fund is currently preparing to transfer the shares to the new shareholders, Transgas with 21.5 percent and Jihomoravska Plynarenska with 10 percent.
- Brno's Efekta Finance purchased shares from KIS, ZB-Trust and SIS to obtain nearly 50 percent of Solo Susice, the largest domestic producer of matches.

- The gross profit of Nova Hut, the largest steel-working firm in the country, has posted profits of 410 million crowns in the first nine months of the year, roughly a third of the 1.2 billion crowns expected in this period.
- Metalimix a.s. is expecting a significant decrease in overall turnover this year. Turnover should decrease from 12 to 13 billion crowns compared to 33.62 billion crowns at the end of 1995.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Establishing forced administration on an investment company or fund is one of the most effective way for the Finance Ministry to combat illegal practices on the capital market since it means a loss of sovereignty for the company.
- The recent announcement that price regulations on petrol will most likely be discontinued in January next year will likely not bring any jump in petrol prices.
- The interest in GSM phones has exceeded even the most optomistic expectations. RadioMobil has obtained 18,000 customers in only two months of operations.
